div.head: ALLEGED ENCROACEDIENT AT SANKEY.
div.p: ALLEGED ENCROACEDIENT AT SANKEY.

The SURVEYOR reported that a serious encroachment on the Broad Oak Green, Sankey, by Messrs. Greenall, Whitley and Company had come to his knowledge. The firm had put down boundary posts, and on measuring them he found there was an encroachment.
After discussion it was decided to request the firm to remove the posts.
THE DANGEROUS STATE OF BUTTERMILK BRIDGE.

The SURVEYOR reported that Buttermilk Bridge was collapsing and was in a very dangerous state. Half of the bridge belonged to the borough and the other half to the District Council but the Borough half was in a far worse condition than the District Council's. When the Council repaired their side the Borough side Dulled it down. He would prepare designs for a new bridge if the Council desired it and the Corporation would con- sent to pay half the cost. It was decided to leave the matter in the hands of the Surveyor who would approach the Corporation and re- port at the next meeting.

div.head: LOCAL WEDDINGS. Brough —Hudson.
div.p: LOCAL WEDDINGS. Brough —Hudson.

A large congregation assembled in Friars' Green Independent Methodist Chapel. on Thursday afternoon on the occasion of the marriage of Mr. Walter Brough second son of Councillor Walter Brough, The Grange. Fearnhead, and Miss Clara Hudson, second daughter of hfr. James Hudson, 38. Parker street, Warrington. The service was conducted by Mr. Robert Henshall and commenced with the singing of the well-known hymn " The voice that breathed o'er Eden." The bride, who wits given away by her father, was becomingly attired in a dress of ivory silk over pink Roman satin. She wore a veil of Brussels net and wreath of orange blossom and carried a lovely shower bouquet of pink roses the gift of the bridegroom. Another gift of the bridegroom was a gold locket set with sapphires and chain. The brides- maids were Miss Mary Hudson (sister of the bride),and Miss Elizabeth Brough (sister of the bridegroom) and , they wore dresses of biscuit muslin with picture hats. Their shower bouquets were composed of tea roses. rho duties of best man were discharged by Mr. Thomas Brough. Mr. Joseph Critchley presided at the organ and at the conclusion of the ceremony played Mendels- sohn's "Wedding March." When the newly-married couple left the chapel they were greeted with a shower of confetti, and received the congratulations of numer- ous friends. A reception was afterwards held in the schoolroom, a large number of guests attending. Later in the day Mr. and Mrs. Walter Brough departed for North Wales where the honeymoon is being spent. The bride's travelling dress was a fawn tweed costume with hutnt straw picture hat.

A Defence that Felted. At the Warrington County Court or Thursday, before his Honour, Judge Bowen Rowlands, K.C. Messrs. W. Hodgkinsoni Ltd., Bridge-street, claimed :£1.6 Os.. from Peter Furness, baker, Knntsford-road, _

for linoleum, carpets. &c., supplied. Evidence was given in support of the claim by Mr. Gilman, clerk, in the employ of the plaintiffs and Mr. Coates, assistant. A youth named William Monks proved the delivery of the goods.—The defendant denied that he ordered the goods or instructed anyone to order them for him. He could not tell whether the goods were in his house or not.—His Honour said the evidence showed that the defendant was, in the shop when the goods were ordered and that he was ptesent when they were delivered. The defendant now wished to persuade him (his Honour) that he did not know what was in his house. He never heard of such a defence, and the defendant ought to be ashamed to . come into Court and make it. He (rave judgment for the plaintiffs.— Mr. Gihnour applied for the money to be paid at the rate of 3:,1 per month.—The defendant said he was only an assistant baker earning 225. a week. He denied that he was a partner in the firm of Furness, Bros.—His Honour ordered the amount to be paid at the rate of 10s. a month. Good Templars' Convention.

The monthly meeting of the No. 1 South-West Lancashire Convention LO.G.T. was held on Saturday last in the Independent Methodist Chapel, Stubshaw Cross, Ashton, Bro. J. Parr, C.C.T., presiding. There was a good attendance of representatives and mem- bers from Leigh, Earlestown, Hindley, Wigan,Widnes, Warrington, St. Helens, and Tyldesley. The usual order of business was gone through, the Secretary's report showing that the Lodges throughoqt the Con- vention area were in a fairly prosperous condition,and that a new lodge was about to be opened at Bamfur- long. The reports of the various representatives were also very encouraging, many reporting fair increases in the membership of their lodges. Bro. J. Schofield D.E. Superintendent (Liverpool), gave a very instruc- tive address on the Compensation question, during which he spoke strongly against any attempt on the part of Parliament to compensate the trade, on the removal of licences, out of public funds and urged upon all present to do their utmost to oppose Mr. • Butcher's Compensation Bill. The following resolution, proposed by Bro. Vint, C.E.S., (Ashton) seconded by Bro. G. Clarke, C. Conn (Earlestown) and supported by Bro. Schofield D C S Liverpool was unanimously adopted. " That this meeting hereby protests against any attempt of Government or Parliament to interfere with the discretionary powers of Justices in discharging their duties as Licensing Magistrates either on suspending or by limiting such power, or by providing compensation. when houses are no longer necessary for the convenience of the public. And that this meeting pledges those present to use every legitimate efforts to prevent Mr. Butcher's Compensation Bill and Sir W. Hart Dyker Suspensory Bill or any other measure of similar importance from becotuing law. And that copies of this Resolution be forwarded to the Honorary Secretary, Prime Minister, Sir H. Campbell Bannerman M. P. and to Colonel R, Pilkington M. P. for Newton Division.—A special district lodge session was held when the district degree was conferred on several members by Bro. Schofield. Votes of thanks were passed to the Aston members for the able manner they entertained the converition also to Bro. Schofield for his address.

div.head: NOTES ON GAMES AND ATHLETICS
div.p: NOTES ON GAMES AND ATHLETICS
tricket.

Cricket was a practical impossibility in thelVarring- ton district on Saturday, rain falling almost con- tinuously during the afternoon. The Warrington team should have met St. Helens at the glass and pill centre but the match had to be abandoned. The only local cricketers who appear to have had the satisfaction of playing a match are Sankey Wire Mills and they journeyed to Platt . Bridge to meet the Primitive Methodists, The home team were victorious by a majority of 30, Taylor (29) being the only Warrington player to attain double figures.

On Moiiday Warrington visited Old Trafford and tried conclusions with the Manchester eleven. The game, resulted in a draw but the home team had by far the best of matters and would probably have been victorious had the Warringtonians been able to conclude their innings. Having compiled 252 for the loss of only 4 wickets the Manchester bats- men declared their innings and Warrington had run, up the total of 03 for the loss of 3 wickets when play ceased.

It is only reasonable to take into consideration that Warrington lacked the services of several prominent players including Messrs. J. W. Bibby, and E. A.. Connor. Lynes, too, had not regained his usual form his injured leg troubling him. Consequently his bmvling was not by any mems up to the standard which we have bacpine used to associate with the pro- fessional. On the other hand Manchester were strongly represented and runs were obtained with comparative ease. T. Ambery wielded the willow in splendid style and knocked up 78 (not out). Heap was almost as successful, his contribution being 70 (not out). E. Rigg was responsible for 44.

W. H. Podmore was Warrington's moit useful bats- man but unfortunately he was compelled to retire with an injured hand when his innings had realized 21. P. B. Hawtiu (14), was the only other player to reach double figures. Manchester's most effective bowler was Webb, who accounted for 2 wickets at a cost of 14 runs. •

Warrington Co-operative encountered St. Helens Co-operative on the latter team's ground on Tuesday and gained the advantage by a margin of 19. Banner was the only player whose score ran into double figures, and he knocked up 12.

div.head: Angling.
div.p: Angling.

The Lynun anglers have put into the arm at Massey Brook another good supply of perch and roach, most of which are sizable fish. The perch will be a wel- come addition to those turned in last year, for until then no fish of this kind were to be caught there.
The next meeting of the committee of the Warring- ton Anglers' Association will be held on Friday, July 10th instead of July 3rd (Walking Day).

The outing of the Latchford A.S. on Saturday last to Stretton was a great success. Under the respec- tive captainship of Messrs. Harry Taylor, president, and 11. Gorton, vice-president, teams were chosen from the members of the club .for a friendly tussle at bowls and the president's team proved victors by the narrow majority of four points. Score, presi- dent's 'team 153. vice-president's team 149. After the games, Mr. J. Broady, host of the Cat and Lion Inn, provided an excellent tea which was much enjoyed.

At the monthly meeting of the Howley A.S. held last Monday evening, it was decided to enter club teams for both the Warrington and Worsley Shield Competitions. The annual match was fixed for Aug : 2nd at Barrow Lock, Northwich. At the meeting of the Traveller's Rest A.S. the federation scheme of the Association was favourably received. The annual match of this club will be fished at Vale Royal on July 26th. The Mersey A.S. will fish their opening matcli. at Vale Royal on June 21st.

The unsatisfactory climaticconditions-vvhich prevailed last week-end somewhat interfered with the comfort of those anglers who ventured out. However, a few fish, trout, were creeled from the Bollin (Association length) and Messrs. Watkinson, Hart, Ellis, Batmen, Nixon, Willis, and Bennion were amongst the success- ful .anglers. The flies, Black Gnat and Red Spinner, have been successful lures on warm evenings when a rise has been observed. Messrs. Nixon and Willis registered gudgeon on the 16th just;, the first day of the season for coarse fish.

div.head: Cycling.
div.p: Cycling.

Dr. Peacocke met with an accident whillt cycling on Monday evening near the Conservative Club. It appears that a clog tip got in his front wheel and jammed the brake. The bicycle tipped up and the doctor was pitched violently on to the footpath, bruis- ing his arm and leg. He was much shaken, but was able to limp home.
C. Berry continues to win prizes on the cycle path. On Saturday, at St. Helens he came in second in the two miles and one mile cycle events.
Foot Racing.

At the sports in connection with the St. Helens Recreation Club on Saturday, H. Watkins, of Latch- ford, was second in the 220 yards fiat race. There were several successful Warrington competitors at the Cheshire Lines sports held at Lostock Gralam on Saturday. In the 120 yards and 200 yards handi- caps, C. Sinclair Carried off the third prizes, and in the half mile handicap, J. Craddock (30 yards) secured the premier prize. There was an 80 yards flat race for ladies, and it is satisfactory to know that Miss G fiirchall was successful in obtaining the third prize:

div.head: GREATER RUNCORN.
div.p: GREATER RUNCORN.
Another Meeting of Halton Ratepayers.

A second meeting of the Halton ratepayers was held in the Parochial School on Tuesday evening "to empower the Parish Council to incur whatever expense is necessary in opposing the proposed amalgamation with Runcorn." Mr. J. S. Jeacock (vice-chairman of : the Parish Council) presided, and a small attendance included Messrs. .1. Manning, J. Walker, S. Povey, B. Haddock, J. Hancock and A. Woodier (clerk to the Council.) The details of the question were thoroughly explained at the last meeting. The pad sh - would be put to some expense in opposing the scheme, but the steps to be taken were for the benefit of the parish, and they hoped they would frustrate the designs of Runcorn. They had no antipathy as individuals to Runcorn, but they liked to retain their independence. They had a Parish Council and a Parochial Committee who could manage theiraffairs economically and well. Mr. Walker proposed 'That ne the ratepayers of the Parish of Halton, in the rural district of Runcorn, assembled ata duly convened meeting in the Parochial School on Tuesday, the 16th day of June 1903, hereby authorize and urge the Parish Council of this parish to strenuously oppose the application of the Urban Dis- trict Council of Runcorn for an extension of their boundary by the inclusion of the plrishes of Halton and Weston within their district., and empower the Parish Counqil to incur any necessary expense in con- nection with such opposition."—Mr. Haddock seconded. He said that the inquiry was fixed for next Tuesday,and he strongly advised every ratepayer who could attend to be the present at the inquiry.He considered, however, that it was being held at a very unfavourable time.— The resolution was then put to the meeting and unani- mously carried.—A vote of thanks was passed to Mr. iJea,cock for presiding, on the motion of Mr. Manning, seconded by Mr. Povey.
A mass meeting of the licensed trade was held at Bur- ton, on T iesday night, Lord Burton. presiding, wh

• ea GP , resolutions were carried urging upon the GovernMent pass this session at least a suspensory Bill hindering magistrates from Confiscating I icenceE, and give a pledge that the matter should be dealt with another year.
